methods.label: Verify the quotient using digit blocks
methods.explanation:
The \(24\) ones in \(R_{24}\) form six blocks of \(1111\), matching the divisor \(R_4\). Multiplying \(1111\) by \(10^4\) shifts its digits four places to the left, exactly one block.

Therefore,
\[
R_4\bigl(1+10^4+10^8+10^{12}+10^{16}+10^{20}\bigr)=R_{24}.
\]
The six shifted copies of \(1111\) occupy separate four-digit blocks and fill all \(24\) positions. No blocks overlap, so no carrying occurs. Since \(R_4=1111\ne0\), this proves that
\[
Q=1+10^4+10^8+10^{12}+10^{16}+10^{20}.
\]
These terms place six ones four positions apart. There are three zeros in each of the five gaps between consecutive ones. The first and last digits are both \(1\), so these gaps contain all the zeros, each counted once. Thus the number of zeros is \(5\cdot3=\boxed{15}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
